proposals.prompt: Choose the four statements that represent Maxwell’s equations: (A) Electric field lines originate on positive charges and terminate on negative charges. (B) Magnetic field lines have no beginning or end. (C) A changing magnetic field induces an electric field. (D) Magnetic fields can be produced by electric currents or changing electric fields. (E) An object maintains constant velocity unless acted on by a net force. (F) Energy is conserved. Which selected statement contains Maxwell’s addition to the theory?
proposals.internal_answer: A–D; D includes changing electric fields as a source of magnetic fields.
proposals.rationale: Preserves multiple-selection format, reduces irrelevant distractors, and asks about Maxwell’s contribution. Directly supported by the four prose laws and next paragraph.

proposals.prompt: Which of the following motions of an electric charge produces electromagnetic radiation: remaining at rest, moving with constant velocity, or oscillating back and forth? Explain what distinguishes the radiating motion from the others.
proposals.internal_answer: Oscillation involves acceleration; an accelerating charge radiates.
proposals.rationale: Removes magnetic-monopole distractor; adds explanation. Supported by explicit accelerated-charge discussion.

proposals.prompt: An electromagnetic wave travels horizontally to the right, and its electric field oscillates vertically. Describe the direction in which its magnetic field oscillates. Explain why this is a transverse wave.
proposals.internal_answer: Magnetic field oscillates perpendicular to both propagation and electric-field axes, into/out of the page for a page-plane diagram. Both fields are perpendicular to propagation.
proposals.rationale: Adaptation of lecture transverse-wave objective; asks geometry without video or quotation recall. No instantaneous field sign requested.

proposals.prompt: Two radio waves travel through vacuum. One has a frequency of 1 MHz and the other 100 MHz. (a) How do their speeds compare? (b) Which has the longer wavelength, and by what factor? Explain without calculating either wavelength separately.
proposals.internal_answer: Same speed c; 1 MHz wave has wavelength 100 times longer.
proposals.rationale: Combines inverse-relation and AM/FM comparison families; given frequencies avoid reliance on broadcasting details.

proposals.prompt: Compare red and blue light traveling through vacuum. Which has the higher frequency? Which has the longer wavelength? How do their speeds compare?
proposals.internal_answer: Blue higher frequency; red longer wavelength; equal speeds c.
proposals.rationale: Extends original red/blue question using spectrum figure and c=fλ. Some reinforcement of previous proportional question; may choose only one if desired.
